# pg_corpus_proj.txt -- surfaces S6 (projection, BOUNDED) and
#                       S7 (getcoords, EXACT)
#
# FROZEN FIXTURE.  Generated by pg_mkcorpus.py.
#
# All coordinates are hex float32 BIT PATTERNS.  A shared decimal parser
# would be a shared divergence, so there is not one.
#
# GRAMMAR
#   PROJ  <id> which=poly3d|polymap nrv= v=x,y,z;... cam= ang= dpp= uneg=
#              colore= flares= entity= draw=
#   ROWUV <id> nrv= v= cam= ang= dpp= i= ipart=
#   GETC  <id> p=x,y,z cam= ang= dpp=
#   FACING<id> v=x,y,z;x,y,z;x,y,z cam= ang= dpp=
#
# dpp defaults to 210.0f (NOCTIS.CPP:2214 followed by
# change_camera_lens()), NOT the header's 200.
#
# BLOCK `EXACT`: dpp=128, camera at the origin, all angles zero, every
# vertex at z=128.  Then every intermediate is dyadic and the screen
# vertex is exactly (x+158, y+100); rzf = 128 >= uneg so doflag == nrv
# and the near-plane walk is bypassed.  Rounding is not exercised at
# all: this block isolates topology from arithmetic.

# --- fst-asymmetry probes ---
# At alfa=beta=0 the rototranslation multiplies by exactly 1 and 0, so
# `fst zz` narrowing is a no-op and the four asymmetry sites are
# UNOBSERVABLE by construction.  These rows use awkward camera offsets
# (so z-cam_z, x-cam_x, y-cam_y are NOT exactly representable in
# binary32) together with non-zero angles (so the products are genuinely
# rounded).  The constants are hand-chosen decimal fractions with long
# binary expansions; they were NOT searched for with the code under
# test, which would make the corpus self-derived.
